Findings

Portfolio-wide strengths & issues

Strengths

  • Manava's site proves the group can build genuinely deep, well-optimized property pages when it invests the effort
  • Real, current, verifiable trust signals exist (2026 TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice at Niu, EarthCheck/RSE/IGLTA at Manava) — they're just not leveraged consistently
  • Consistent NAP and phone/email patterns across properties support entity grounding for AI models
  • Club Tiare (Air Tahiti Nui) loyalty partnership is consistently represented at the properties that display it

Issues

  • Three different booking engines mean three different guest experiences and three vendor relationships to manage
  • Niu Beach's single-page architecture is the most severe structural issue in the portfolio — no separately indexable pages at all
  • Reva Tahiti has no English-language site despite serving international travelers, with English inquiries routed to a separate outsourced domain
  • Image alt text is inconsistent-to-absent across all four sites
  • Zero properties have an llms.txt or structured FAQ content built for AI answer engines
  • Stale content exists at multiple properties (Reva marked "coming soon" on corporate despite being open; a stale pre-rebrand Booking.com link on Manava)
Methodology: Scores are a manual structural audit based on direct fetches of each live domain, not an automated crawler score. The same seven-factor SEO rubric and six-factor AIO rubric were applied to all four properties for comparability. Elements like JSON-LD structured data live in page <head> markup that isn't visible through structural fetching and should be confirmed separately via a schema validator before finalizing client-facing claims. Core Web Vitals figures are directional; a live PageSpeed Insights/CrUX run is recommended per domain before quoting exact performance numbers.
